Definition: of Latin origin; a modius, i.e. certain measure for things dry (the quantity or the utensil):--bushel.
BiblicalUsage: A modios is a bushel measure, a basket for grain — and Jesus uses it for a lamp: no one lights a candle and puts it under a bushel, but on a candlestick, so it gives light to all in the house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bushel is a warning against hidden faith: light is given to be set out, not stored.
